problem: Suppose that $N$ can be written in base $6$ as $531340_6$ and in base $8$ as $124154_8$. In base $10$, what is the remainder when $N$ is divided by $210$?
solution:
The prime factorization of $210 = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5 \cdot 7$. By the Chinese Remainder Theorem, it suffices to find the residues of $N$ modulo $5$, $6$, and $7$. Since the units digit of $N$ in base $6$ is equal to $0$, it follows that $N$ is divisible by $6$. Also, we note that $N$ is congruent modulo $b-1$ to the sum of its base $b$ digits. Indeed, if $N$ can be represented as $(\overline{a_ka_{k-1}\cdots a_0})_b$, then \begin{align*}N &\equiv a_k \cdot b^k + a_{k-1} \cdot b^{k-1} + \cdots + a_1 \cdot b + a_0 \\ &\equiv a_k \cdot ((b-1) + 1)^k + \cdots + a_1 \cdot ((b-1) + 1) + a_0 \\
& \equiv a_k + a_{k-1} + \cdots + a_1 + a_0 \pmod{b-1}.
\end{align*}It follows that $N \equiv 5+3+1+3+4+0 \equiv 1 \pmod{5}$ and that $N \equiv 1 + 2 + 4 + 1 + 5 + 4 \equiv 3 \pmod{7}.$ By the Chinese Remainder Theorem and inspection, we determine that $N \equiv 31 \pmod{35}$, so that (by the Chinese Remainder Theorem again) $N \equiv \boxed{66} \pmod{210}$.
response_with_ans:
We have \begin{align*}
N &= 531340_6 \\
&= 5\cdot6^5 + 3\cdot6^4 + 1\cdot6^3 + 3\cdot6^2 + 4\cdot6^1 + 0\cdot6^0,
\end{align*}so reducing modulo 7, we get \begin{align*}
N &\equiv 5\cdot(-1)^5 + 3\cdot(-1)^4 + 1\cdot(-1)^3 + 3\cdot(-1)^2 + 4\cdot(-1)^1 + 0\cdot(-1)^0 \\
&\equiv -5 + 3 - 1 + 3 - 4 \\
&\equiv \boxed{4} \pmod{7}.
\end{align*}Also, \begin{align*}
N &= 124154_8 \\
&= 1\cdot8^5 + 2\cdot8^4 + 4\cdot8^3 + 1\cdot8^2 + 5\cdot8^1 + 4\cdot8^0,
\end{align*}so reducing modulo 5, we get \begin{align*}
N &\equiv 1\cdot3^5 + 2\cdot3^4 + 4\cdot3^3 + 1\cdot3^2 + 5\cdot3^1 + 4\cdot3^0 \\
&\equiv 243 + 162 + 108 + 9 + 15 + 4 \\
&\equiv 3 \pmod{5}.
\end{align*}Finally, \begin{align*}
N &= 1\cdot8^5 + 2\cdot8^4 + 4\cdot8^3 + 1\cdot8^2 + 5\cdot8^1 + 4\cdot8^0,
\end{align*}so reducing modulo 3, we get \begin{align*}
N &\equiv 1\cdot(-1)^5 + 2\cdot(-1)^4 + 4\cdot(-1)^3 + 1\cdot(-1)^2 + 5\cdot(-1)^1 + 4\cdot(-1)^0 \\
&\equiv -1 + 2 - 4 + 1 - 5 + 4 \\
&\equiv 0 \pmod{3}.
\end{align*}Therefore, $N$ has a remainder of 4 when divided by 7, a remainder of 3 when divided by 5, and a remainder of 0 when divided by 3. By the Chinese Remainder Theorem, there is a unique residue class modulo $3\cdot5\cdot7 = 105$, and hence modulo 210, that satisfies these conditions. Checking the values $3 + 5k$ for $k = 0,1,2,\ldots,6$, we find that only $3 + 5\cdot5 = 28$ is congruent to 4 modulo 7. Thus, $N$ has a remainder of $\boxed{28}$ when divided by 210.
